sections.context: Bash Boilerplate is a shell script framework with core.sh (30+ utility functions), main.sh (argument parsing + main logic), build.sh (generates standalone.sh), and standalone.sh (single-file distribution). Tests use bats-core with only 3 functions covered out of 70+. The project uses Seeds for issue tracking and Warren for PR delivery.
sections.reproduction: 1. Compare core.sh timestamp() (line 361) with standalone.sh timestamp() (line 362) — they differ. 2. Run wait_for_url() with set -e enabled — the ((c++)) at c=0 returns exit code 1, terminating the script. 3. Run retry() with complex quoted arguments — eval mangles argument boundaries. 4. Read timestamp() doc comment — it claims ARGS: $1 (optional) but the function takes zero args. 5. Run tests — only is_sourced, slugify, and is_int are tested. 6. Create a symlink /tmp/<script>.lock -> /etc/cron.d/malicious — lock() would follow it.
sections.root_cause: standalone.sh was generated from an older version of core.sh and never regenerated. wait_for_url() uses ((c++)) (post-increment) which returns 0/exit code 1 when c=0 — a classic Bash arithmetic pitfall with set -e. retry() uses eval on a space-joined string, losing argument boundaries. Doc comments were written before the function signature was finalized. Tests were never expanded beyond smoke tests. lock() uses predictable /tmp paths without atomic file creation.
sections.approach: Six findings to fix: (1) regenerate standalone.sh from current core.sh+main.sh, (2) fix wait_for_url() ((c++)) bug that terminates script under set -e, (3) fix retry() argument boundary loss via eval, (4) fix timestamp() doc comment drift, (5) add tests for untested public functions, (6) harden lock() against symlink attacks.

steps.title: Regenerate standalone.sh from current core.sh and main.sh
Fix wait_for_url() ((c++)) — use pre-increment or arithmetic to avoid set -e exit
Fix retry() argument boundary loss — pass args as array instead of eval string
Fix timestamp() doc comment — remove incorrect ARGS claim
Add missing tests for untested public functions in core.sh
Harden lock() against symlink attacks — use mktemp or flock

acceptance: standalone.sh regenerates cleanly and matches core.sh content
retry() preserves argument boundaries for complex commands
timestamp() doc comment accurately reflects zero arguments
test suite covers all critical public functions
lock() uses mktemp or flock for atomic, unpredictable lock files
